players.note: Travis Kelce is the TE7 in fantasy points per game with a 16.4% target share, 2.34 YPRR, two red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.1% first-read share. On a per-route basis, he has been excellent. Among 48 qualifying tight ends, he ranks fourth-best in yards per route run and sixth-best in first downs per route run. Kelce should have a strong week against a pass defense that has allowed the ninth-most yards per target to tight ends.

Tucker Kraft is warming up. Over the last two weeks, he has been the TE8 in fantasy points per game. In those games, Kraft has had a 68.8% route share with a 19.7% target share, 2.41 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 25.5% first-read share. Kraft is due for a big week. This could be it. Dallas has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Despite last week's stinker, Juwan Johnson is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. Johnson has a 14.6% target share with 1.59 YPRR, seven red zone targets, one deep target, and an 18.4% first-read share. New York has been a tougher matchup for tight ends, holding the position to the sixth-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. I lean on the side that their prowess against the position is more real than illusion after they held Trey McBride to seven receptions (12 targets) and only 31 receiving yards. Johnson will need a score this week to pay off for fantasy.

After starting the season with two monster games, Dalton Kincaid has gone silent. He hasn't had more than 3.8 PPR points over the last three games. Joe Brady talked about getting him more involved moving forward, but we'll see if that starts this week. This would be a great matchup to do so, though. Kincaid has a 15.2% target share (64.5% route share or higher in four of five games) with 2.74 YPRR, one red zone target, three deep targets, and a 16.9% first-read share. The Raiders are 16th in yards per target allowed to tight ends, but against the position they have also given up the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game, the third-most receiving touchdowns, and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity. Kincaid could feast this week.

Harold Fannin Jr. is the TE13 in fantasy points per game. He has earned a 17.6% target share with 1.09 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 15.2% first-read share. Fannin could see more work this week with KC Concepcion possibly out (concussion). Baltimore has faced the fourth-fewest tight end targets while allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends (three scores). Fannin could be a TE1 this week.

In his two full games this season, Dallas Goedert has finished as the TE3 and TE11 in weekly scoring. In those games, Goedert has had a 21.5% target share with 2.17 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 23.3% first-read share. Goedert should have another strong TE1 week. Carolina has allowed the eighth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Goedert's median projection and ceiling take a small hit with Tanner McKee under center this week, but he's still a strong play.

Brenton Strange is the TE14 in fantasy points per game with at least 10.3 PPR points in three of five games this season. Among 47 qualifying tight ends, Strange is eighth in target share (18.2%), sixth in YPRR (2.12), tenth in FD/RR (0.099) and sixth in first-read share (20.8%). Strange has three red zone targets and one deep target. Strange has been amazing on a per-route basis and has emerged as the consistent number two target for Trevor Lawrence. Strange could be a TE1 again this week. Houston has allowed the 12th-most yards per target to tight ends while facing the sixth-fewest targets to the position (tied).

This hurts to type, but Colston Loveland is the TE36 in fantasy points per game. Good lawd, this is frustrating. To see him heavily involved in Week 4 and tank last week was tough. Overall, Loveland has a 70.2% route share, a 12.8% target share, 0.79 YPRR, six red zone targets, and an 18.7% first-read share. It feels like another middling week for Loveland against the Falcons. This week, he faces an Atlanta secondary that has the fourth-highest single high rate (64%). Against single high, Loveland has only a 14% target-per-route run rate with 0.67 YPRR. Atlanta has allowed the 13th-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity. I'm likely streaming a tight end over starting Loveland this week, but as has been the Bears all season, watch him pop off with a good game despite the analytics stacked against him.

Pat Freiermuth is a popular streaming tight end option for Week 6, and I'm going against the consensus and fading him this week. Last week, Freiermuth exploded with two scores as the TE4 for the week, leaving him as the TE10 in fantasy points per game for the season. Muth has a 13.4% target share, 1.30 YPRR, five red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 15.4% first-read share. The matchup on paper looks good for Muth, but the coverage structure isn't in his favor at all. Tampa Bay has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Tampa Bay has the second-highest rate of single-high in the NFL (65.2%). Freiermuth has been one of their go-tos against two-high and usually non-existent vs. single-high. Against two-high, Freiermuth has a 29% target-per-route run rate and 2.12 YPRR, but against single-high he has only a 12% target-per-route run rate and 0.80 YPRR. Even going all the way back to 2025, Freiermuth has only had a 15% target-per-route run rate against single-high with 0.84 YPRR. Freiermuth will need a touchdown to likely save his fantasy day this week because I'm not projecting an encore of last week's game in Week 6.

Over the last two weeks, Tyler Higbee has finished as the TE12 and TE10 in weekly scoring. In those two games, Higbee has had a 68.8% route share, an 11.4% target share, 2.0 YPRR, zero red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 13.9% first-read share. He could easily be a TE1 again this week. Arizona has allowed the most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

With Mark Andrews solid per-route stats, it's kinda surprising that he has been a fantasy disappointment as the TE19 in fantasy points per game. Among 47 qualifying tight ends, Andrews is fourth in target share (21.9%), 16th in YPRR (1.64), ninth in first downs per route run (0.102), and fourth in first-read share (25.5%). Andrews has only one score while having five red zone targets and one deep target. Andrews could be a TE1 this week, but I think it's more likely he has a down week. Cleveland has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target to tight ends while ranking 17th in fantasy points per opportunity to position.

Dalton Schultz is seemingly being phased out of the Houston passing attack. I don't know why, but it is happening. Schultz's route share has dropped in every game this season from 73.8% in Week 1 to only 44.4% last week. Since Week 3, Schultz has had only a 10.9% target share, 1.21 YPRR, and a 12.7% first-read share. In those three games, he has still seen three red zone targets and two deep targets. Schultz isn't a fantasy option this week. The Jags have held tight ends to the seventh-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Hunter Henry has been a fantasy ghost as the TE25 in fantasy points per game this season. Henry has posted double-digit PPR points in only one game. He has only a 11.5% target share with 1.53 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 14.4% first-read share. Henry isn't on the streaming radar this week. The Jets have held tight ends to the eighth-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Kyle Pitts' playing time has been volatile this season. In his five games played, he has two weeks with route shares under 50% and three games with at least a 64% route share. In two of those outings, he had at least a 70% route share. One of those games was last week. Pitts has an 11.2% target share (17% TPRR) with 1.22 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and an 11.9% first-read share. Pitts is on the streaming radar this week against a Bears defense that has defended the fewest tight end targets in the NFL, but they have allowed the tenth-most yards per target to the position. Pitts could flirt with TE1 production this week, but he could also be a nothingburger in your lineup.

Jake Ferguson is a touchdown-or-bust tight end option. Ferguson is the TE23 in fantasy points per game with a 10.9% target share, 0.73 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 9.9% first-read share. Sit Ferguson again this week. Green Bay has limited tight ends to the fifth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Darren Waller has seen his route share increase weekly with Carolina from 37.2% in Week 1 to 62.2% in Week 4. Excluding Week 1, as he had only a 37.2% route share, Waller has had an 18% target-per-route run rate, an 11.2% target share, 1.54 YPRR, three red zone targets, zero deep targets, and an 11.8% first-read share. Waller isn't on the streaming radar this week, though. Philly has held tight ends to the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity and zero receiving touchdowns.

AJ Barner is the TE30 in fantasy points per game with only one game this season with more than double-digit PPR points, but he's on the streaming radar this week. Barner has a 13.6% target share with 1.07 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 13.7% first-read share. Barner's touchdown equity in the passing offense is palpable. Denver has been vulnerable to tight ends, giving up the 12th-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Barner could post low-end TE1 numbers this week.

With Brock Bowers in the lineup, Michael Mayer has had a 10.7% target share, 1.40 YPRR, one red zone target, and an 8.6% first-read share. In those three games, Mayer has one TE1 finish in weekly scoring (TE7). Mayer is on the streaming radar this week. Buffalo has allowed the 11th-highest yards per target to tight ends while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity given up to the position.

Yes, I know you were expecting to see Pat Freiermuth's name here, but I lean toward Darnell Washington having the busier day in Week 6. This goes back to Tampa Bay's love of single high and how Pittsburgh has deployed these tight ends. Tampa Bay has the second-highest rate of single-high in the NFL (65.2%). Against single-high, Washington leads the team with a 25% target per route run rate with 2.0 YPRR. Freiermuth has been one of their go-tos against two-high and usually non-existent vs. single-high. Against two high, Friermuth has a 29% target per route run rate and 2.12 YPRR, but against single high he has only a 12% target per route run rate and 0.80 YPRR. Overall, Washington has a 65.3% snap rate and only a 35.8% route share with an 8.6% target share (22% TPRR), 1.79 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 10.3% first-read share. With the Steelers short on wide receivers and the coverage matchup, I could see Washington having a surprising game as a wonderful streaming option. Tampa Bay has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Washington was a TE1 in Week 4 (TE12). He could be a TE1 again this week.
